acceptance_walk:
Bench "review-l4-chat-answers" (daemon 48991, UI 2591), started from my worktree at c41bfdd. I ran three walks and looked at every screenshot. Kept under /tmp/frbench/review-l4-chat-answers/keep/ (walk1-steps, walk2-steps, walk3-steps, walk1.json); the walk JSONs are /tmp/frbench/review-l4-chat-answers/walk2-first.json, walk2-restart.json and walk3.json. All bench homes are deleted and no bench is running.

Walk 1 (--provider bench, FORERUNNER_BENCH_CHAT_NOLOOK=1), with projects Notes and Site:
- In Site's Chat: "add a task: write the README". Then I renamed it with `tool: task_update` and pressed Yes, so it became "Write the guide" (01-03).
- In Notes' Chat:
  - "add a task to Site: write the shop page" gave 'Added "Write the shop page" to Site.' (04).
  - "switch to Site" gave "Switched the active project to Site. This chat stays about Notes.", and the tab stayed on Notes. The bubble also shows a second line, "Switched the active project to Site. [Undo]" (05). See blocking 3.
  - "add a task there: write the about page" landed in Site (06). Site's tasks: Write the guide, Write the shop page, Write the about page. Notes has none.
  - "open Site" and "open it" both navigated to /projects/<Site>/chat (07, 08).
  - "add a task to re-check the prices" gave "Which project: Notes or Site? Options: Notes, Site." (09). Pressing Notes sent "Notes" to the model, a paid call, and no task was added (10). "add a task to fix the login: users cannot sign in" asked the same question (11). See blocking 1.
  - "say: Shall I set research ...?" was nudged, then replaced by "Nothing changed, and nothing waits for your yes. Say it again to try once more." (12). A typed "yes" then got 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes. Say what you want done, for example "run it now" to start a session.' with 0 model calls (13).
  - A read-back the model wrote itself was nudged and replaced (14).
  - A forged "The app did: ..." line was stripped, leaving "[stand-in model]" (15). The claim guard did not fire here, because the stand-in's "[stand-in model]" prefix stops `^The app did:` from matching.
  - A reply with paragraphs and a list, posted via POST /chat and read after a reload, renders as separate paragraphs and a list of two items (16).
- In Site's Chat: "what happened to the README task?" In the model-call log (seq 9-11), the stand-in first said "There is no record ... Should I look ...?", the ABSENT_NUDGE followed, then a recall call. The answer was 'From the record of Sun 22 Nov: Write the guide: Ready. Earlier called "Write the README".' with "From: Write the guide (22 Nov)" for a hit it never opened, and the From line stays after a reload (17, 18).

Parser probe (a temporary vitest file, since deleted) on base and on the fix with projects Notes and Site:
- Base adds a task for "add a task to re-check the prices", "... to e-mail Anna about the opening hours", "... to follow-up with the printer", "... to fix the login: users cannot sign in", "... to write the README: explain how to open the page", "... to clean up - remove the old files" and "... in two weeks: renew the domain".
- The fix asks "Which project: Notes or Site?" for every one of them.

blocking.issue: L4-selftasks-119's target-project reading breaks ordinary 'add a task …' lines (U-015). A hyphen inside a word, or a colon or dash after 1 to 3 words that name no project, now asks 'Which project: …?' and adds nothing. The option button does not finish the add either: it sends the bare name to the chat model, a paid call that adds no task. With one project the question reads 'Which project: Notes?'.
blocking.evidence: Bench walk 1, steps 09-11: in Notes' own Chat, 'add a task to re-check the prices' gives 'Which project: Notes or Site? Options: Notes, Site.'. Pressing Notes sends 'Notes' to the model (model-call log seq 2: '[stand-in model] I was given …') and the header still reads 'No tasks yet'. 'add a task to fix the login: users cannot sign in' asks the same. Walk 3 step w3-01, with one project: 'Which project: Notes? Options: Notes.'. Parser probe: base adds 'Re-check the prices', 'E-mail Anna about the opening hours', 'Follow-up with the printer', 'Fix the login: users cannot sign in', 'Clean up - remove the old files' and 'In two weeks: renew the domain'; the fix asks a question for each. The target regex accepts `[:,-]` with no space before it, so 're-check' splits into the target 're' and the title 'check the prices'. addTarget then asks for any unknown target of 1 to 3 words after to/in/into. The spec allows a question only for a pronoun target with no project switched to ('a pronoun target … resolves … or chat asks'), and fix_scope says 'Without the separator today's reading stays'.
blocking.expected: Only a real separator counts: a colon or comma, or a dash with a space before it. Words after 'to/in/into' that name no project keep today's reading: the task with those words, acting at once with Undo. 'Which project: …?' is asked only for a pronoun ('there', 'it', 'dort') with no project switched to, and only with two or more projects. If a question is asked, pressing an option must finish the add in that project, not send the name to the model. Add intent.test.ts cases for 're-check', 'e-mail', 'follow-up', 'fix the login: …' and one project, plus a real-daemon or UI case for the option press.

blocking.issue: The new 'asks' claim catches clarifying questions. Each one gets a nudge, and if the model asks again its question is replaced by 'Nothing changed, and nothing waits for your yes. Say it again to try once more.'. This breaks the area's own decision ('Clarifying questions stay free') and the L4-selftasks-119 decision, under which chat asks 'Which project: Notes or Site?'.
blocking.evidence: claimsOf probe: 'Which task should I add it to?' is asks ('should I add'). 'Add it to Notes or to Site?', 'Start it now or wait for the next session?' and 'Run the tests first?' are asks by the read-back pattern. 'Should I start with the shop page or the about page?' is asks. Bench walk 3 steps w3-02 and w3-03: 'Which task should I add the note to?' and 'Add it to Notes or to Site?' reach the person as 'Nothing changed, and nothing waits for your yes. Say it again to try once more.', at 2 model calls per turn (4 chat calls in total). The read-back pattern skips which-questions, but the 'shall/should/can I <verb>' and 'do you want me to <verb>' patterns do not, and no pattern skips either/or questions. The acceptance's only negative case is 'Which project do you mean?'.
blocking.expected: A question that asks which, who, where or what, or offers a choice ('X or Y?'), is not an 'asks' claim under any ASKS pattern. claimOf returns null for 'Which task should I add it to?', 'Add it to Notes or to Site?' and 'Should I start with the shop page or the about page?' (unit cases), plus one composed case where such a reply reaches the person unchanged with one model call.

blocking.issue: 'switch to Site' in another project's Chat tab now shows the same sentence twice in one bubble: 'Switched the active project to Site. This chat stays about Notes.' and below it the change line 'Switched the active project to Site. [Undo]'. Before this change it showed once.
blocking.evidence: Bench walk 1 step 05 (walk1-steps/05-05-notes-switch-to-site.png). The fixer's own after-screenshot /tmp/frbench/fix-l4-chat-answers/steps/02-after-02-switch-to-site.txt shows the same two lines; the before-screenshot (before-steps/02-before-02-switch-to-site.txt) shows one. Cause: the extra clause makes the reply text differ from the action's sentence, so Conversation.tsx's showText check (sentences.includes(text)) no longer folds it into the change line. Design §5 rule 10 (one place per fact) and §3.9 ('Undo.' never doubled next to the button) apply. active-project.test.tsx only checks toHaveTextContent, so it misses this.
blocking.expected: The bubble says the switch once, with its Undo, and adds 'This chat stays about Notes.' once. For example, carry the clause in the action's sentence, or have the UI fold a reply that is the action's sentence plus that clause. A UI test should assert the sentence appears exactly once.

non_blocking: The forged-line guard: CHANGED's `^The app did:` does not allow a leading bracket prefix, though the read-back ASKS pattern does. On the bench the stand-in's '[stand-in model] The app did: …' was stripped without a nudge. withoutAppMarkers is also case-sensitive, so 'the app did: paused it' passes through. Neither case is shown as a marker, but the bench never walks the guard.

'absent' false positives: 'I don't see any failed tasks.' in a 'what is left?' answer is an absence claim, so it costs one extra nudge and a recall call. The answer stands and the cost stays inside the turn budget.

The user guide says 'a change you ask for always comes back as the app's question with Yes and No'. If the model asks in words again after the nudge, the reply is 'Nothing changed, …' instead, so the sentence promises more than the code does (§5 rule 9). Reword it, for example to 'is read back by the app with Yes and No'.
The user guide does not mention 'add a task to <project>: …', 'open <project>' or 'This chat stays about <tab>'.
'Nothing changed, and nothing waits for your yes. Say it again to try once more.' reads oddly when the person asked for no change, as in a status question the model answered with 'Shall I …?'.

namedProjectId is the registry's active project whenever any earlier turn in this conversation switched. If the person later switches the active project from the header, 'there' means that project, not the one the conversation named.

Commits 95f8992, 40aed74 and bf4542a add real-daemon cases for changed POST /chat behaviour, but the fake daemon's chat does not play 'add a task to Site: …' or recall sources. The route shape is unchanged, so this is only a gap in the stand-in for UI tests.

Parser questions repeat their options in the text and as buttons ('Which project: Notes or Site? Options: Notes, Site.' plus Notes and Site buttons). This predates the area, but the new add-task question inherits it.

For the session lead's live check (final_check): ask a real fast model a clarifying-type request (for example 'add a note to the task') and confirm the answer is not replaced. Also try 'add a task to re-check the prices' once blocking 1 is fixed.
